title: Inline Function

solutions.title: Three rules, not seventeen functions
solutions.tradeoff: The policy now lives as a five-line boolean chain plus three named rules; a reader who wants to unit-test the suspension or age check in isolation can no longer do so without exporting a function that exists only to be inlined again.

reviewFocus: Did every purely single-field alias - isSuspended, getRunnerAge, getQualifyingSeconds and the rest - actually disappear, or did one survive out of habit?
Is meetsQualifyingTime still the only helper with a branch in it? If a second helper grew an if, ask whether it should have stayed inlined instead.
Does hasRequiredConsent still read runner.age >= 18, not 18 >= runner.age or some other transposition that would silently flip who needs consent?
Count the functions left in src/. Four is the defensible number; ten is a sign half the inlining did not happen.

Is the double negative in meetsLicenseRequirement (!course.requiresLicense || runner.hasClubLicense) still expressed as an implication, or did the solution try to simplify it into a form that reads correctly but tests the wrong thing?
